company_info.company_description: "Replenishable Energy offers quality materials, brand name products, knowledgeable advice and a minimum warranty period of five years on your whole solar system. We’re committed to industry best practice and providing you with a truly comprehensive solar service, at the very best price.We deliver solar solutions for a wide range of residential, rural and commercial customers, across Cairns and its surrounding areas, including all of Queensland. Our friendly, professional team of Cairns solar specialists will guide you through every stage of your solar journey, from initial enquiry, to site inspection, system design and final installation. We can even assist with repairs and maintenance, as and when needed.We are an NETCC approved seller, which means when you choose us, you can be assured that you’re buying a quality product from a company that follows all relevant consumer protection laws and implements best solar industry practice at all times. Our team includes licensed electricians and SAA Accredited Solar Installers. Our services provide you with the peace of mind you deserve. Our products have been specifically chosen and designed to perform in our tough conditions."

Living in FNQ and expecting a 30% price rise in the next few months I finally bit the bullet and installed a large solar and battery system a couple of months ago.When seeking quotes I had 2 requirements, blackout protection and zero power bills.After eliminating all the cookie cuter quotes from other suppliers that ignored my above request I settled on Replenishable Energy who installed a Sungrow Hybrid system consisting of the following:28kW of Solar (68 x Trina 415W panels)2 x Sungrow 10kW Hybrid inverters one with a 16kWh Sungrow Battery and the other ready for a second battery module if I decide to upgrade in 12 months.My previous power bills were around $2500 a year at the current Ergon rate and they were expected to go up to at least $3250 after the rise.I elected to remove the Gas HWS which was costing around $1000 per year in gas and put in a 3.6kW 400L Electric HWS, This was set on a timer to run from 11am to 3pm.The pool filter now runs from 10am to 3pm and we delay start the dishwasher to start at around 10am each day.I also replaced my gas stove with an inverter cooktop.And to facilitate max export Replenishable upgraded the switchboard to 3 phase.Total cost was for the solar install was around 40k (including the Solar install and 3 phase upgrade)I had a pretty good idea what I wanted but what really sold me with Replenishable Energy was having Rollo come over and take the time to give my wife detailed explanations on everything in relation to the install and our options on how to achieve what we wanted with the system.So far I am happy with the system performance:During winter (FNQ Winter that is LOL) with the batteries I don't draw from the grid at all and export between 60-90kWh a day to the grid with the batteries currently charging from about 630 to 930am.We had a few hot end of summer days when it was first installed where the 16kWh battery would last until about 930pm each night and the grid would feed us overnight consuming about 20kWh from the grid while running 2 x 6kw house ACs in the afternoon to about 730 and 4 x 2.5kw room ACs overnight. The battery is usually charged fully by 930 each morning.These hot days eat a bit into my feed in especially on the weekend but I still manage to come out on top, the second battery I am considering will eliminate this grid draw completely.Rough calculations, currently by saving $3500/year in electricity and Gas and making around $1000/year from FIT it should have paid for itself in around 12 Years. (less than 10 years if you take in consideration the upcoming price rises.)

The rep was very straightforward and quoted on exactly what we wanted (he also gave us some very helpful advice on work to undertake on our roof beforehand, later independently backed up by a local builder; none of the other companies did this)2. RE managed to hit a sweet spot for us between price, quality and warranty (esp. in terms of basic panel brand and warranty)3. The quote was also very straightforward didn't over-promise on the performance of the final product4. RE were the only company to recommend an install under cover in the car port; all the other Reps suggested next to the fusebox in partial shade (presumably as they wouldn't need to run the cabling through the roof for this)4. The team were polite and friendly and cleaned up afterwards.Our only criticism would be around the lead time between the deposit and commencement of the work, and the scheduling of this installation.  We feel that the RE rep could have been a little more realistic about how soon work would likely commence after the contracts were finalised.  We signed off on the contract in late November, and while we were told that we had missed out on a slot before Christmas, we were given an approximate date of just after Christmas.  This ended up being late January, right at the end of the school holidays.  We were also not told that RE would be closing down for a fortnight over Christmas/New Year.  However, we also accept that it is difficult to schedule work around this time of year, particularly during rainy season in FNQ, and that our expectations of an early Jan install may have been unrealistic.Once we made contact after RE re-opened, they seemed to do their best to try and commence as soon as they were able. We were given approximately 24 hours notice of the installation occurring, but were able to work with our employers to accommodate this.Grid connection occurred very soon after the install and we have had no further issues or concerns since turning the system on.We have now had the system installed and operational since late Jan and have had two monthly bills from Ergon.  We are *extremely* happy with the results.  Our Feb bill dropped from $220 in 2020 to $24 in 2021, and our March bill fell from $200 to $4.26.  We have also substantially increased out daytime power usage over this period.The Fronius app is also very easy to use and has helped us understand how best to adjust out power use to reduce our usage.Overall, we are very happy with our system and our choice of installer.  We would strongly recommend Replenishable Energy to anyone in the Cairns/FNQ region.
